gaps.note: Commercial break edit, hides time elapsed.

stage_a.note: Enthusiastic and confident delivery of the product reveal with a clear smile.
Sustained engaged excitement about the device's capabilities and mission.
Friendly, approachable orientation, handing out champagne to the panel.

venture.description: A smartphone breathalyzer that plugs into the audio jack to measure blood alcohol content and promote smarter decisions.
venture.note: The product includes a hardware sensor and a mobile application.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Presents the Breathometer, a smartphone breathalyzer, asks for $250k for 10%, and demonstrates it by pouring champagne for the panel.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if the product is already on the market and currently being sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains they launched in March via Indiegogo, sold 4,000 units in 30 days, and generated $140,000 in revenue.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Clarifies for the panel that Indiegogo is a crowdfunding platform similar to Kickstarter.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks what the retail price of the unit is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the price is 49.99.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks if they can see the device.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees to show the device.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Challenges the founder on the huge liability of someone relying on the device and then getting arrested or causing harm.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that the device promotes smarter decisions, includes disclaimers and an instruction manual, keeping the company legally clear.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if she should come up and try the device.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Invites her to come up.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Jokes that her ability to walk in heels will give away her sobriety level.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Guides her through plugging in the device, hitting start, and blowing, then reads her result as .04.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Notes that her reading would be legal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms she is legal to drive.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks if the device can also tell if she has bad breath.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Reveals they are looking into a sensor for halitosis and are focusing on a less intrusive diabetes test next.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks about his background, whether he is a software or hardware design guy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mentions he used to code and sold his last company within 18 months before developing Breathometer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks why he didn't invest his own money from his previous successful exit into this venture.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms he invested an initial 50k and has already raised half a million from angel investors.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks what the requested investment money will be used for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the money will be used strictly for manufacturing the product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Notes that Europe, Canada, and Mexico are moving toward zero tolerance, asking if that is the trend.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that it is the trend.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mentions that they just lowered the limit from .08 to .05.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Expresses being a big fan of the sensor business and sees it as the future of technology.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: States he is going to make an offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Offers $500,000 for 20% of the company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Adds that he will give the founder a chance to talk to the other investors.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks Mark if he would let her join his offer to handle retail.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Declines, stating he is not worried about retail compared to the long-term benefit.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Offers $250,000 for 15% so the founder loses less equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Acknowledges that the offer is not bad.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Points out his offer is much less dilutive than Mark's.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Proposes opening up the round to involve more than one shark to close a full $1 million round.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Suggests letting the sharks do the whole round.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms that is exactly what he is proposing.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: States he does not want to work with the other sharks.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Checks if he wants to raise a million dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms he does want to raise a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Argues that Mark is not giving him enough money.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Replies that he is not done talking yet.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Offers another $250,000 if Kevin will let him join.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Agrees to let Robert join the offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Offers to add another $250,000 to the group.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Clarifies that the group's equity total is 30%.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Teases that the others have no idea what they are investing in.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Summarizes the group offer as $750,000 for 30%.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Comments that it is smart to surround oneself with smarter people.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Offers to match the original ask of $250,000 for 10% plus unlimited manufacturing.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks Daymond if he wants to partake in the group.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Explains that getting everyone together is hard and they don't need all those people.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Points out that right now they cannot agree.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Suggests they can agree if they raise the dollar amount.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Suggests a million dollars of straight equity to get all the sharks in.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Adds they need a significant discount to do it, which would be an unbelievable story.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that it would be an unbelievable story.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Tells Mark he needs the lion's share because competing is expensive versus colluding.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: States he is willing to go in if Cuban is in, giving the founder all five sharks.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what the lion's share means and what equity he would get.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tells Mark he gets all five sharks and needs a million bucks today, asking Mark to sell him.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Presses the founder for what he can give on a straight equity deal for the whole round.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Urges Charles to think.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Tells him he has to come up with a really good offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Counters by asking if Mark would take 300k while the others split the remaining 700k.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Revises his offer to $500,000 for 15%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Acknowledges the 15%.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Proposes all five sharks give $1 million: Mark gets $500k for 15%, the others split $500k for 15%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hesitates.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Urges him to do it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reminds him the champagne is open for a reason.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Asks for a second to call his CFO.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Agrees.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tells his CFO they have an offer from all five sharks for a million dollars for 30%.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Notes that a million for 30% is a $3.3 million valuation, which is not huge.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Expresses worry about too many cooks in the kitchen and big egos working together effectively.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Bets that the founder will come back asking for 25%.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Agrees he will say 25%.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Says they will see what happens.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Reiterates the deal: $1 million total, Mark takes $500k for 15%, the rest split $500k for 15%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts the offer.

turns.speaker: PANEL
turns.summary: The panel cheers and congratulates him with hugs and a champagne toast.

exchanges.label: tease about not knowing the product

decisions.note: Robert proposes a syndicate of all 5 sharks.

record.notes: Commercial break edit at 7:19. F1 speaks to F2 (CFO) on the phone during the negotiation.
